Meta.title: Overlap
Meta.description: Meet the people your campus life already overlaps with.

Home.title: Overlap
Home.tagline: Meet the people your campus life already overlaps with.
Home.whatBody: We introduce you to people based on campus life you actually overlap with — the same class, the same club, similar free time. Not just a photo to swipe past, but a reason you'd get along.
Home.whyBody: Instead of endless swiping, we introduce 6 carefully picked people every day at noon. Each one comes with the reasons you overlap, so you can find people who actually share your interests, faster.
Home.safetyBody: Only verified students can be matched with, and you can block or report anyone at any time. When it's time to meet, we suggest public spots on campus.
Home.statusNote: We're still building this. Join the waitlist and we'll email you the moment we open.

terms.intro: These Terms set out the conditions for using Overlap (the "Service"), provided by the operator (legal entity to be designated, owner task O1; the "Company").

purpose.heading: 1. Purpose of the Service
purpose.body: The Service helps students on the same campus find friends, study partners and dates based on shared courses, clubs, free time and interests. It is free and is not a paid matchmaking service.

eligibility.heading: 2. Eligibility
eligibility.body: Only people who are 19 or older, hold a campus email address (.ac.kr), and pass identity checks (age verification, photo verification) may use the Service. Minors may not use it.

accounts.heading: 3. Accounts and verification
accounts.body: Each email address may create only one account. Verification selfies are deleted within 7 days of a moderator's decision; only a "verified" flag remains afterward. A banned account's identity is retained only as an irreversible hash, to prevent re-registration.

obligations.heading: 4. User obligations
obligations.body: You must follow the Community Guidelines. Capturing, sharing or distributing another user's photos or conversations without consent; creating, distributing or possessing non-consensual intimate images or deepfakes (a criminal offense, subject to immediate permanent ban and evidence preservation); commercial advertising, spam or contact-list uploads; and registering false information are all prohibited.

datingMode.heading: 5. Dating mode and sensitive information
datingMode.body: "Who I'd like to meet" reveals sexual orientation, which is sensitive information, and is only collected with separate, explicit consent. Declining it still leaves Friends and Study Buddy modes available; only Dating mode is unavailable. Recommendations are rule-based; see the How matching works page for details.

content.heading: 6. Rights in content
content.body: You retain the rights to photos, prompt answers and other content you post. The Company uses it only as needed to provide the Service (recommendations, profile display). Content confirmed to violate the Guidelines after a report may be removed.

enforcement.heading: 7. Enforcement and account restrictions
enforcement.body: Violations follow a warning → 7-day suspension → permanent ban ladder. Every suspension or ban is decided by a human moderator with a stated reason, and you can appeal it; no account is suspended or banned by an algorithm alone. Serious violations such as non-consensual images or deepfakes can result in an immediate permanent ban without going through the earlier steps.

serviceChanges.heading: 8. Changes to and termination of the Service
serviceChanges.body: The Company may change or discontinue parts of the Service with advance notice. You may delete your account at any time; deleted data is handled per the retention table in the Privacy Policy.

liability.heading: 9. Limitation of liability
liability.body: The Service is a tool for helping people meet and does not guarantee any outcome. In-person meetups happen at your own responsibility; see the Safety page for guidance the Company provides.

disputes.heading: 10. Dispute resolution and jurisdiction
disputes.body: These Terms are governed by the laws of the Republic of Korea. The competent court will be specified once the operating entity is designated (to be confirmed).

termsChanges.heading: 11. Changes to these Terms
termsChanges.body: Changes are announced in advance; changes that materially affect your rights require renewed consent.

contact.heading: 12. Contact
contact.body: Please use the CPO contact listed in the Privacy Policy (designation pending).

privacy.intro: Overlap collects, uses, stores and deletes personal information under this policy. The processor and cross-border transfer register also lives in docs/data-flow.md and is kept identical to the table below.

whatWeCollect.heading: 1. What we collect and why
whatWeCollect.body: We collect the items in the table below for signup, profile creation, matching and safety operations. We never collect resident registration numbers or CI.

sensitiveConsent.heading: 2. Separate consent for sensitive information
sensitiveConsent.body: "Who I'd like to meet" (sexual orientation) and, if introduced, an automated face-comparison result (biometric data) are collected only with separate, explicit consent. Declining leaves the rest of the Service available. This data is field-level encrypted, never displayed, and used only for matching.

automatedProcessing.heading: 3. Automated processing notice
automatedProcessing.body: Daily picks are decided by a rule-based algorithm we run on our own servers, not by a person browsing profiles and not by generative AI. See How matching works for the signals used and why, and you have the right to ask for an explanation or a human review of a specific recommendation (PIPA Art. 37-2).

chatAndReports.heading: 4. Chat and report handling
chatAndReports.body: No one reads chat content as a matter of course. When a report is filed, a moderator reviews only the recent messages (up to 50) the reporter themselves attaches — this is the only way chat content ever reaches a human. Uploaded photos are automatically screened for inappropriate content; chat text is checked only against in-house spam/scam/phone-number patterns and is never sent to an outside service.

CommunityGuidelines.title: Community Guidelines
CommunityGuidelines.intro: Overlap is a space for students on the same campus to meet with respect for each other. These rules apply to everyone, and breaking them can lead to anything from a warning to a permanent ban.
CommunityGuidelines.respectBody: Take "no" or silence as an answer. Continuing to contact someone after they've blocked or hidden you, or trying to get around a block or hide setting, is against the rules.
CommunityGuidelines.prohibitedImages: Taking or sharing photos or videos without consent, and non-consensual intimate images or deepfakes (making, distributing or even just possessing them is a criminal offense and results in an immediate ban and a report).
CommunityGuidelines.prohibitedCapture: Screenshotting another user's photos, profile or conversations and taking them outside the Service.
CommunityGuidelines.prohibitedHarassment: Harassment, threats, hate speech, sexual harassment.
CommunityGuidelines.prohibitedSpam: Spam, scams, pushing people to outside links or phone numbers, commercial advertising, asking people to upload contact lists.
CommunityGuidelines.prohibitedImpersonation: Impersonating someone else, fake profiles, use by minors.
CommunityGuidelines.enforcementTitle: What happens if you break a rule
CommunityGuidelines.enforcementBody: Violations follow a warning → 7-day suspension → permanent ban ladder. Every suspension and ban is decided by a moderator who reviews the reason personally, and you can appeal it. Serious violations like non-consensual images or deepfakes can go straight to a permanent ban without the earlier steps.
CommunityGuidelines.reportingBody: You can report from any card, message or profile in two taps. Reporting immediately hides you from the other person, and urgent reports (non-consensual images, deepfakes, threats) are reviewed within 2 hours. See the Safety page for more.

Safety.title: Safety
Safety.intro: Some guidance for staying safe while chatting online and meeting up in person.
Safety.beforeMeetingVerify: Check that the other person is verified, and get to know them a bit before agreeing to meet up.
Safety.beforeMeetingPlanner: Use the meetup planner (coming soon) to pick a time from your shared free windows and a place from the curated safe-spots list.
Safety.beforeMeetingShare: Use "Share my plans" (coming soon) to let someone you trust know your first name, the place and the time. It never shares your precise location.
Safety.duringMeetingBody: Meet in a public place with other people around, and it's always okay to leave if something feels off. You don't need to rush to share private details like your home address, student ID or exact class schedule.
Safety.afterMeetingBody: You can leave a quick note on how it went in the app, and choosing "made me uncomfortable" takes you straight into the report flow.
Safety.reportBody: You can report or block from any card, message or profile in two taps. Blocking makes you invisible to each other, permanently unless you undo it. You can also hide yourself from specific courses, clubs or email addresses. See the Community Guidelines for the full rules.
Safety.emergencyDigitalSexCrime: Digital sex-crime victim support center — for non-consensual images and deepfakes
Safety.emergencyCampus: Campus security and sexual-violence/human-rights center contacts vary by school and will be added here once campus data is registered (to be confirmed).

HowMatchingWorks.title: How matching works
HowMatchingWorks.intro: Your daily picks are chosen by a set of rules we run on our own servers — not by a person browsing profiles, and not by machine learning or generative AI. Every match is based on things you and the other person both entered: your courses, clubs, free time, interests and a short values quiz.
HowMatchingWorks.signalCourses: Shared courses — sharing a small class counts for more than sharing something everyone takes.
HowMatchingWorks.signalClubs: Shared clubs and organizations, weighted the same way.
HowMatchingWorks.signalTime: Overlapping free time, plus any hangout spots you've both opted into.
HowMatchingWorks.signalInterests: Shared interests from the tag list — rarer interests count for more.
HowMatchingWorks.signalValues: How close your answers are on the 8-item values quiz.
HowMatchingWorks.weightsTitle: It depends on what you're looking for
HowMatchingWorks.weightsBody: Which of these matters most changes with the mode you're browsing in: study buddy leans on shared courses and free time; friends leans on clubs and interests; dating weighs values and interests more heavily. A match only counts if it looks good from both sides — one person being a great fit for the other isn't enough on its own.
HowMatchingWorks.batchBody: Every day at noon we put together 6 people per mode you're active in: your 4 best matches, one person ranked a bit further down the list so you don't only ever see the same kind of profile, and one recent newcomer. No one profile can appear in more than 25 people's picks on the same day, so early or popular profiles don't crowd everyone else out.
HowMatchingWorks.explanationsBody: Each pick shows up to 3 concrete reasons — the specific course, club, interest, free-time overlap or values fit behind the score. We only ever show something you both actually have; nothing about anyone's private preferences is ever revealed this way.
HowMatchingWorks.rightsBody: This is an automated process, which you have the right to ask about. If you'd like an explanation for a specific match, or a human to review how your picks are put together, contact us and we'll follow up.
